name: AutoPlay
tagline: Turns SVG artwork into finished educational videos and publishes them to your YouTube channel.
about: AutoPlay is a video automation tool. It takes SVG artwork and animation clips, runs them through an automated pipeline to a finished timeline, and renders the result as a video.
When a video is ready, AutoPlay can publish it to a YouTube channel you've connected, with its title, description and thumbnail.
features: Build videos from SVG artwork and a library of animation clips
Automate every step, from the brief to the rendered video
Publish to one or more of your YouTube channels
howItWorks: AutoPlay runs on your own computer. It has no server of its own: it talks to Google directly, and nothing it handles is sent to {owner}.
data: Your YouTube channel's basic details, such as its name and ID
Details of the videos on your channel, such as their titles and status
The video files, titles, descriptions and thumbnails you choose to publish
sharing: AutoPlay doesn't sell your information, use it for advertising, or share it with anyone. It sends information only to Google, to carry out what you ask it to do.
storage: When you connect a channel, Google issues a sign-in token. AutoPlay saves it in a file in its credentials folder on your computer, and sends it only to Google. Channel and video details are used while AutoPlay runs and aren't stored anywhere else.
delete: To remove the saved token too, delete the token file in AutoPlay's credentials folder on your computer.

scopes.label: Manage your YouTube videos
scopes.use: Upload the videos you choose to publish, with their titles and descriptions.

scopes.label: Manage your YouTube account
scopes.use: Read your channel's details and your videos' details, and set the thumbnail of each video AutoPlay uploads.
